svg.title: WP-V-03 Figure 2-1: the known scenarios
svg.desc: Known scenarios: SC-01 Pedestrian on or stepping onto a marked crosswalk: passes when No contact with the pedestrian; the vehicle yields as the traffic rules require, and the monitor commands the deceleration that restores the safe distance whenever Autoware does not; unjustified hard braking counts against the SOTIF acceptance criteria; SC-02 Pedestrian emerging from behind a parked vehicle: passes when The vehicle's speed near the occlusion lets it stop for a road user emerging at the assumed speed; no contact, and no swerve out of the drivable area to avoid one; SC-03 Vehicle ahead braking or stopping in congested traffic: passes when No collision with the vehicle ahead; acceleration stays inside the envelope, the monitor restores the safe longitudinal distance, and a braking shortfall on a wet road switches to the secondary path; SC-04 Spurious obstacle with a road user following: passes when Braking that the safety channel does not confirm stays at or below the firm level; emergency braking happens only when a road user is confirmed; a blocked safety sensor is detected and Autoware stops comfortably; the belt warning acts; SC-05 Signalised intersection with cross traffic: passes when The vehicle enters only on a recognised green and treats an unknown signal as red; whatever the signal, it does not enter when its swept path crosses that of a detected road user before it could stop or clear; SC-06 Unprotected left turn across oncoming traffic: passes when The vehicle starts the turn only with a gap that lets the oncoming road user pass at its assumed speed and acceleration, and stops before the conflict area otherwise; SC-07 Entry to a roundabout with traffic circulating: passes when The vehicle yields to circulating traffic and enters only with a gap that its assumed speed allows; SC-08 Cyclist alongside on the inside of a turn: passes when No steering command whose swept path comes within the safe lateral distance of the cyclist is executed; the vehicle waits or stops in lane; SC-09 Lane keeping where localisation is degraded: passes when The vehicle stays in its lane and drivable area; a steering command toward a detected road user or kerb is rejected and the vehicle stops in lane; a degraded pose is detected; SC-10 Work zone or re-marked lanes not yet in the map: passes when The divergence monitor detects the disagreement and the vehicle carries out a minimal risk manoeuvre; it never follows the map into a closed lane; SC-11 Person directing traffic: passes when The vehicle detects the person directing traffic, stops safely and asks for remote assistance; it does not move on the signal alone, and responders can stop or hold it; SC-12 Emergency vehicle approaching with siren and lights: passes when The vehicle detects the emergency vehicle, pulls to the side when safe or stops, and lets it pass; when it cannot yield it reaches a minimal risk condition; SC-13 Rare object or debris in the lane: passes when The vehicle stops before the object or passes it within the lane when clear; a vehicle that cannot find a way on reaches a minimal risk condition and asks for help; SC-14 Weather changing toward the ODD limits during a trip: passes when The weather monitor detects the exit, treats a reading it cannot tell from the limit as outside, and the vehicle reaches a minimal risk condition; detection inside the ODD still meets the safety channel's requirement; SC-15 Kerbside stop while passengers board or alight: passes when The vehicle does not move with a door open or a person in the near field in the direction of travel, never reverses, and resumes only when every release condition holds; SC-16 Stopped at a red light with pedestrians crossing in front: passes when The vehicle stays held until every release condition holds; motion while holding is detected and the park brake applied; no acceleration toward a detected road user; SC-17 Loss of Autoware while driving: passes when The monitor detects the loss within its detection budget and stops the vehicle in lane with hazard lights on, without Autoware; a fault of the monitor itself leads to the vehicle's own stop, never to the park brake while moving; SC-18 Pull-over minimal risk manoeuvre along a busy kerb: passes when The vehicle pulls over only into a mapped safe stopping place and stops in lane otherwise; repeated stop requests go to a remote operator; SC-19 Passengers leaving at a stop in lane: passes when The vehicle holds the minimal risk condition with hazard lights on and warns passengers of traffic on their side before they leave; the residual risk counts against the SOTIF acceptance criteria; SC-20 Remote driving with a delayed or lost link: passes when Commands older than the age bound, out of sequence or failing their integrity check are rejected and the vehicle stops; the envelope checks apply to remote commands as to Autoware's; a remote emergency stop brakes firmly unless the safety channel confirms a road user; SC-21 Remote release of the wrong vehicle or at the wrong moment: passes when A release moves the vehicle only when it is bound to that vehicle, authentic and fresh, and the release conditions hold; SC-22 Turn indicator during a turn or lane change: passes when The indicator always matches the commanded and achieved steering direction; on a mismatch hazard lights come on; SC-23 Give and take with other drivers: passes when The vehicle takes its turn as the rules give it and shows when it yields and when it is about to move; its hesitations and stops count against the SOTIF acceptance criteria; SC-24 Passenger misuse and emergencies in the cabin: passes when No control is reachable from the cabin; every seat reaches a remote operator who can divert the vehicle; no trip ends with a person inside without an operator's decision; SC-25 First responders at a collision: passes when The vehicle stops and holds after a collision; doors open from inside without power; responders can find the isolation points and reach remote operations; SC-26 Return to service after maintenance: passes when The vehicle refuses driverless dispatch until calibration, cleanliness and versions are checked and recorded; parameter changes outside the release process are rejected.
svg.text: What each known scenario sets up, and when it passes
WP-V-03 §2, Figure 2-1: one concrete instance of each logical scenario, what it exercises, the ODD attributes it varies, its methods and pass criterion,
and the verification cases of WP-S-09 that run it. Schematic: the ranges are in §2.2, and no scenario has been run.
